column3: It mirrors the group-led arrival, opened gates, and gatekeeper speech in the contrary Garden outcome.
A clear messenger having come frames the focus question about whether warning reached its hearers.
God's word establishing truth gives a broader counterpart to the punishment-word becoming due.
It closely repeats the post-judgment question about messengers, recited signs, warning of this Day, and self-incriminating reply.
The immediate next ayah turns arrival at Hell's gates into the command of permanent entry.
It identifies the messenger as a warner, the role recalled by Hell's gatekeepers.
Those confronted with the Fire answer yes to its truth and are then told to taste punishment for disbelief.
Hearing speech and following its best form provides the receptive opposite to the focus's admitted rejection.
Creation in truth does not add to the arrival, warning, or judgment exchange.
Hell's keepers question each incoming group about a warner, directly clarifying the focus's gatekeeper interrogation.
Every soul arrives with a driver and witness, expanding the compelled arrival before judgment.
Its opening is victory, not the opening of Hell's gates or the ensuing accountability.
The accused acknowledge the truth before their Lord and are sentenced to taste punishment for disbelief.
The command to worship and give thanks does not add to this judgment scene.
The repeated sending of messengers establishes the mission whose delivery is queried at Hell's gate.
It joins rejection of God's signs to gathering disbelievers in Hell, without the focus's arrival dialogue.
It defines the messenger's role as bearer of good news and warning, one part of the gatekeepers' question.
An opened heavenly gate and persistent denial offer only a distant gate-and-rejection parallel.
It states that the Lord's word became due upon disbelievers because they are companions of the Fire.
The adjacent Garden response supplies the answered promise and settled abode opposite the focus's condemned arrival.
It explains messengers as bearers of good news and warning and contrasts belief with fearlessness.
A forced acknowledgment is followed by an explanation of self-deception until God's command arrived.
Fear of the Hereafter and hope for mercy provide a same-surah contrast to the focus's terminal fear.
The true Day and return to the Lord frame the meeting-day warning made explicit in the focus.
Forgetting the meeting of this Day is answered with the Fire as an unassisted final abode.
The possibility of a warner in every town expands the reach of the warning whose absence is denied in the focus.
A messenger reciting purified pages gives only a limited counterpart to messengers reciting divine signs.
It closely matches messengers from among people reciting God's signs, and states the saving alternative of mindfulness and reform.
It links disbelief to personal accountability, return to the Lord, and disclosure of deeds within the same surah.
The Lord's word becoming due upon persistent deviants supplies a close judgment principle for the focus's punishment-word.
Earlier peoples received messengers with clear proofs and explicitly rejected what they brought.
The word's continued delivery for remembrance is a broad antecedent to recited signs and warning.
Limits on a messenger's claims do not clarify the focus's warning or final judgment.
Hell's keepers ask its people whether messengers brought clear proofs; their yes answer directly parallels the focus.
The immediately preceding scene establishes the book, prophets, witnesses, and judgment in truth before the groups are driven.
It directs disbelievers toward the Day they will meet and be struck, a narrower counterpart to the warned meeting-day.
Neglecting the meeting of this Day is answered with enduring punishment, directly explaining the focus's warning.
It restates the messenger's warning function, without the focus's later acknowledgment and sentence.
An opened gate leads into severe punishment and despair, making opening an irreversible punitive threshold.
Clear signs are recited to disbelievers who react with hostility, and the Fire is promised as their destination.
The following ayah completes the same-surah judgment tableau with angels, true judgment, and universal praise.
The moon following the sun does not add to the focus's warning or judgment sequence.
Arrival at Hell triggers testimony from the offenders' own faculties, expanding the accountability at the destination.
The command to enter Hell's gates permanently closely supplies the terminal action following the focus.
False partners denying their worshipers are a general judgment confrontation, not this warning-and-arrival scene.
Past disbelievers tasted the consequence of their conduct and still face painful punishment.
Same-surah disbelief after received favor is linked directly to becoming companions of the Fire.
The condemnation of human ingratitude gives only a broad moral description of disbelief.
People already in the Fire address Hell's keepers, extending the gatekeeper relationship after entry.
Its catalog of rewarded faithful qualities is only a broad contrary outcome to the condemned groups.
Signs and warnings do not avail a people who will not believe, explaining why prior warning did not avert the focus's end.
The opening associated with Gog and Magog does not clarify Hell's gates or the warning exchange.
The challenge to powerless intercessors does not add to the focus's arrival or admission.
It states that entrenched disbelievers are neither forgiven nor guided, without the focus's judicial sequence.
Disbelief after submission is paired with painful punishment in this world and the next.
The warning that association nullifies deeds gives a same-surah cause of loss but not this scene.
The bodily crisis image does not add to group driving, warning, or Hell.
It directly names those upon whom the punishment-word is due and locates them in the Fire.
Entering through a gate is a distant contrast because this is a hesitant earthly entry.
Speaking a grave falsehood without knowledge gives a general portrait of the disbelief behind judgment.
A messenger is sent to every community, while some incur misguidance and the deniers' end is displayed.
The reward of good-doers does not add beyond the already-recorded Garden contrast.
Universal denial of messengers is followed by punishment becoming due, closely matching the focus's causal sequence.
The Lord's word becoming due upon people who will not believe closely parallels the focus's formula.
Entering through a gate for victory is a remote contrary use of the entry image.
Disbelievers hasten toward the caller and call the Day difficult, a partial arrival-to-judgment parallel.
The departed multitude restored to life does not clarify the focus's warning or destination.
The erasure of evil deeds and reward of good deeds is only a same-surah contrary outcome.
Disbelievers rushing forward lacks the destination, gate, warning, or judgment of the focus.
Approaching houses through doors offers only a remote doorway image.
It makes prior warning a condition of just destruction, directly grounding the gatekeepers' question.
The prohibition on despair in God's mercy does not add to this final accountability scene.
Those too proud for worship will enter Hell humiliated, supplying a direct entry-and-cause parallel.
The revealed book affects hearers with fear and guidance, contrasting the focus's rejected recited signs.
The concise report that Ad denied the messengers supplies a recurrent historical instance of the focus's charge.
Messengers announce a coming punishment in a different narrative, without the focus's judgment structure.
An enduring word left for descendants to return offers only a broad alternative to persistent disbelief.
The truth's arrival and confirmation of messengers oppose the rejection recalled at Hell's gates.
The same-surah address says the signs came, were denied, and were met with arrogance and disbelief.
Truth's arrival and falsehood's passing are a broad contrary principle, not the focus's warning scene.
Disbelief and obstructing God's way cause works to fail, a general consequence without the focus's route.
Rejecting truth that came and expelling the messenger adds a concrete worldly expression of the focus's disbelief.
Opened heavenly gates releasing rain do not clarify the gates or destination of Hell.
Ad's denial is tied to the question of punishment and warnings, a historical corroboration of the focus's charge.
Angels receive the protected with the promised Day, a deliberate contrary reception to Hell's gatekeepers.
The Prophet did not dwell among Midian reciting the signs but is sent, supporting messenger-mediated delivery.
Entering a gate in humility for forgiveness is a distant inverse of the focus's condemned entry.
The completed Lord's word to fill Hell with jinn and humans directly parallels the focus's fulfilled punishment-word.
Knowing God's favor and then denying it identifies a recognition-to-rejection pattern within disbelief.
The command to taste punishment because of disbelief supplies the retributive consequence without the arrival scene.
Its family-maintenance rules do not add to the focus ayah.
The prior divine word concerning sent messengers gives a broader word-and-messenger counterpart.
Its warning not to disbelieve amid harmful teaching does not clarify the final gatekeeper exchange.
The Messenger is explicitly a clear warner, directly supporting the function invoked in the focus.
When truth came, it was called magic and rejected, supplying a concise pattern behind the focus's disbelief.
Revelation reaches the Prophet's heart so that he may be among the warners, clarifying warning's transmission.
A distinct legal punishment for violent corruption does not explain the focus's eschatological entry.
The question about the Day of Decision reinforces the gravity of the Day whose meeting was warned.
The reminder of blessings and prophets does not add to the focus's gate and judgment sequence.
The Prophet is sent as witness, bearer of good news, and warner, restating the mission recalled by the gatekeepers.
Those who deny God's signs and act arrogantly are explicitly identified as companions of the Fire.
Each community enters the Fire with another, directly supplying the focus's group-based destination.
The criminals appear bound in chains on that Day, expanding the compelled character of their final procession.
Hell is displayed before the disbelievers, a direct prelude to their arrival at it.
Those with light scales remain in Hell, supplying an accountability basis for the final abode.
A blazing Fire is prepared for those who deny the Hour, linking denial to the prepared destination.
Being thrown bound into a narrow place of the Fire expands the irreversible confinement after entry.
The wicked are returned to the Fire whenever they seek to leave and are told to taste what they denied.
Disbelievers remain in Hell without death or reduction of its punishment, clarifying the finality of entry.
The promised Hell is directly addressed to its entrants because of their disbelief.
The wrongdoers are gathered and directed toward the path of Hell before being stopped for questioning.
A return to the blazing Fire supplies a further compelled-destination image.
The arrogant are assigned a dwelling in Hell, directly identifying the destination's occupants in the same surah.
Every soul is fully repaid for its deeds immediately before the focus's group procession.
Those who deny the Book and what came through messengers are seized in a direct counterpart to the focus's charge.
Shackles and chains accompany the condemned, expanding the coercive movement toward punishment.
The chained are dragged through boiling water and then burned in the Fire, completing the punitive route.
God's enemies are gathered toward the Fire and held in ranks, closely paralleling the focus's grouped driving.
The Fire is their abiding place whether they endure it or seek pardon.
The guilty remain permanently in Hell, reinforcing the finality of the focus's destination.
The inhabitants of Hell call to its keeper Malik, extending the focus's keeper-mediated encounter.
The condemned are seized and dragged into the midst of Hell, a close forced-entry parallel.
Hearing God's verses and persisting arrogantly describes the prior response behind the focus's admission.
Each stubborn denier is commanded to be cast into Hell, supplying a direct sentencing action.
The address to Hell on the Day of Judgment frames it as the destination being filled.
On that Day the disbelievers are thrust forcefully into the Fire of Hell.
The Fire they denied is identified at the moment of confrontation.
The Fire becomes the hypocrites' and disbelievers' refuge, a direct final-abode statement.
Hell has stern angelic keepers who do not disobey God's command, directly clarifying the gatekeepers' office.
Disbelievers have the punishment of Hell, the destination whose keepers speak in 67:8 and the focus.
The entrants answer that a warner came but they denied him, the exact fuller response to the focus's question.
The condemned admit that listening or reasoning would have kept them from being companions of the Blaze.
The command to bind the condemned and chain him gives a sentencing counterpart to being driven to Hell.
The command to burn the condemned in Hell directly states the destination's punitive action.
The threat to cast the rejecter into Saqar provides a concise Fire-sentence parallel.
The guardians of the Fire are made angels, directly supplementing the focus's Hell keepers.
Hell is an ambush for transgressors, framing it as the appointed destination.
Hell is displayed for whoever sees, closely accompanying the public realization of final judgment.
Transgression and preferring worldly life are given as the path whose refuge is Hell.
The kindling of Hell supplies a compact eschatological setting for its receiving occupants.
Those barred from their Lord will burn in Hell, linking exclusion with the final fire.
Faces enter a blazing Fire, a compact arrival-and-destination parallel.
Hell is brought on the Day of judgment, making the final destination publicly present.
Disbelievers are assigned the Fire of Hell as permanent dwellers, directly confirming the terminal outcome.
